\begin{frame}{Appendix --- Gender Incidence: How the Split Is Built}
\hypertarget{app:gender}{}
\scriptsize
\textbf{The construct.} $\text{female\_winner\_share} = \text{winner\_share} \times \mathbf{1}[\text{winner is female}]$, \textbf{zero} (not missing) when the winner is a man --- symmetrically for male, and for the runner-up's slot. Two properties follow. \textbf{(i)} Female $+$ male $=$ the total exactly ($0.080+0.527=0.607$ winner; $0.057+0.280=0.337$ runner-up --- the shares on \hyperlink{src:spine1}{\beamergotobutton{the headline}}), $N=\NMunis$ in every column: these columns \emph{decompose} the headline, they are not a new sample. \textbf{(ii)} Nothing is conditioned on --- the tempting alternative, the mean share \emph{among} races where a woman placed second, selects on an outcome of the same shock. The price is that each component mixes an \textbf{extensive} margin (how often a woman holds the slot, isolated by ``runner-up is female'') with an \textbf{intensive} one, so the pair is read together.

\medskip
\textbf{(a) Decomposition.} Female $+$ male reproduce the winner and runner-up totals column by column.
\begin{center}
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\input{../tables/tex/executive_iv_gender_consolidation.tex}}
\end{center}
\medskip
\footnotesize \hyperlink{app:gendergap}{\beamergotobutton{(b) the differential tests}}\hfill\hyperlink{src:gender}{\beamerreturnbutton{Back to the gender split}}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Appendix --- Gender Incidence: the Differential Tests}
\hypertarget{app:gendergap}{}
\scriptsize
The female$-$male gap in each slot, estimated as its \emph{own} outcome rather than inferred from the two component columns. This is the honest test, and it is not decoration: reading a gendered effect off the contrast between a \emph{starred} male component in (a) and an \emph{unstarred} female one is the difference-in-significance fallacy --- two estimates can sit on opposite sides of a significance threshold while the difference between them is nowhere near significant. That is exactly what happens here. The male winner's gain clears at 5\% and the female winner's does not, yet the gap between them carries $p=\WinGapP$; the runner-up slot's gap, by contrast, is a \emph{precisely estimated} zero ($\RUGapCoef$, SE $\RUGapSE$), which is a positive finding rather than an absence of one.

\medskip
\textbf{(b) Differential tests.}
\begin{center}
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\input{../tables/tex/executive_iv_gender_gap.tex}}
\end{center}
\medskip
\footnotesize The last two columns give the net and extensive-margin readings: women's share of the top two, and how often the runner-up slot is held by a woman.
\hfill\hyperlink{app:gender}{\beamerreturnbutton{Back to (a)}}\,\hyperlink{src:gender}{\beamerreturnbutton{Back to the gender split}}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Appendix --- The Council Race Is the Placebo Office: (Almost) Untouched}
\hypertarget{app:councilplacebo}{}
\small
The same instrument, built once from the executive design, applied to the council (vereador) race is a near-complete null: a large, fluid, multi-seat proportional contest absorbs the same litigation with almost no compositional trace. The asymmetry is exactly what front-runner reinforcement predicts --- it bites in the single-winner mayoral race, not the multi-seat proportional one.
\smallskip
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=0.42\textheight,keepaspectratio]{../figures/legislative_coefplot.pdf}
\end{center}
\smallskip
\takeaway{Eight of nine council outcomes straddle zero at 5\%. The lone exception is the \emph{elected} female share ($+0.022$, $p=.036$), with the elected higher-ed share marginal at 10\% ($p=.084$) --- a flicker that does not survive the multiple-testing correction the consolidation clears, so we read the council as the placebo it is designed to be. Candidate pool, party mix, and elected renewal are otherwise unmoved.}\hfill\hyperlink{app:legislative}{\beamergotobutton{Full legislative tables}}\,\hyperlink{app:ballotcouncil}{\beamergotobutton{council ballot}}\,\hyperlink{src:voterballot}{\beamerreturnbutton{Back}}

\begin{frame}{Appendix --- Turnout Placebo (compulsory vote)}
\hypertarget{app:turnoutplacebo}{}
\small
Turnout is one act per voter, so it is office-invariant and reported here on its own. Because voting is \textbf{compulsory} in Brazil, overall turnout is mechanically pinned and \emph{cannot} respond to litigation --- it is a \textbf{placebo}. A near-zero, insignificant coefficient is exactly what a valid design should deliver: the instrument is not picking up some omitted municipal shock that moves all electoral behaviour at once. The elastic, \emph{facultative} turnout margins that \emph{can} move are tested separately \hyperlink{src:turnoutprofile}{\beamergotobutton{by voter profile}}.

\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Appendix --- Voter Behaviour: Turnout by Voter Profile}
\hypertarget{src:turnoutprofile}{}
\small
Compulsory turnout is mechanically frozen, but turnout among the \textbf{facultative} electorate (ages 16--17 and 70$+$) is free to move (it rose from \TurnoutRateTwenty\% to \TurnoutRateFortyFour\% overall, with far larger municipal swings), and turnout has a strong \textbf{education gradient}. If litigation demobilises, these elastic margins are where it should show. Each dot is the 2SLS effect of a one-SD shock; bars are 90\% (thick) and weak-IV (tF, thin) intervals. From the TSE \emph{perfil do eleitorado}; state FE, clustered by state.
\smallskip
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=0.48\textheight,keepaspectratio]{../figures/turnout_coefplot.pdf}
\end{center}
\smallskip
\footnotesize \textbf{Null on every margin.} Every interval crosses zero and the magnitudes are negligible: a one-SD rise in judicialization ($\approx\TreatSDMult\times$ more litigation) moves facultative turnout by only $\FacultativePerSDSigned$~pp and the education gap by $\EduGapPerSDSigned$~pp, both indistinguishable from zero. The high-education margin is closest to a signal ($p=\HighEdP$) but does not clear conventional significance.\hfill\hyperlink{app:turnoutprofile}{\beamergotobutton{Full table}}
\end{frame}
